goal: Review ASP.NET Core code for authorization, model binding, CSRF, CORS, security headers and error handling.
use: Review ASP.NET Core code for authorization, model binding, CSRF, CORS, security headers and error handling. Use when asked to review or harden an ASP.NET Core application or API.

steps.note: Read the app setup. Open Program.cs or Startup.cs, the middleware order, the controllers or minimal API routes, and appsettings.
Check authorization. Every endpoint that changes data or returns private data needs `[Authorize]` or an explicit policy.
Check input binding. Flag models bound directly from the request with no validation, binding of fields the user should not set (such as `IsAdmin`), and missing `[ApiController]` validation.
Check CSRF and CORS. Cookie-authenticated forms need antiforgery tokens.
Check headers and transport. Look for HTTPS redirection, HSTS outside development, and missing security headers such as Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options.
Check errors. Flag exception details or stack traces returned to clients, and `UseDeveloperExceptionPage` enabled in production.

protocol.title: Read the app setup
protocol.text: Open Program.cs or Startup.cs, the middleware order, the controllers or minimal API routes, and appsettings. Note whether the app is an API, MVC or Razor Pages.

protocol.title: Check authorization
protocol.text: Every endpoint that changes data or returns private data needs `[Authorize]` or an explicit policy. Flag `[AllowAnonymous]` on sensitive endpoints, and missing authorization on minimal API routes.

protocol.title: Check input binding
protocol.text: Flag models bound directly from the request with no validation, binding of fields the user should not set (such as `IsAdmin`), and missing `[ApiController]` validation.

protocol.title: Check CSRF and CORS
protocol.text: Cookie-authenticated forms need antiforgery tokens. Flag `AllowAnyOrigin` combined with credentials, and wildcard origins.

protocol.title: Check headers and transport
protocol.text: Look for HTTPS redirection, HSTS outside development, and missing security headers such as Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options.

protocol.title: Check errors
protocol.text: Flag exception details or stack traces returned to clients, and `UseDeveloperExceptionPage` enabled in production.

protocol.title: Check output
protocol.text: Razor output that is not encoded, `Html.Raw` on user data, and JSON responses that include internal fields.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: List each finding as `file:line`, with severity (high, medium or low), the problem and the fix. Mark what you did not run.
